name: The four māras of Chöd
description: The obstructive māra (sense objects that provoke attachment and aversion), the unobstructive māra (arising thoughts), the māra of elation (attachment to attainments and good fortune) and the māra of conceit (self-fixation), the root of the others.
antidotes: cutting self-fixation by the view of emptiness

equivalents.note: same name, different set: the classical four are the aggregates, afflictions, death and the divine son

name: Ego-clinging (bdag 'dzin)
description: Grasping at a self: in Chöd the real demon and root of the four māras; in Sowa Rigpa the ignorance at the root of the three poisons and of all disease.

equivalents.note: self-grasping as the root of faults
equivalents.standpoint: Buddhist analysis of the root affliction

name: Spirit harm (gdon)
description: Harm from spirits: in Sowa Rigpa a condition and a class of disease requiring ritual; in Chöd, beings to be fed and repaid rather than fought.

name: Imbalance of the three nyepa
description: Increase, decrease or disturbance of rlung, mkhris pa or bad kan — alone, in pairs or all together — which is disease.

name: Rlung disorders
description: Disturbance of wind: restlessness, sleeplessness, dizziness, wandering thoughts and pains that move; cold in nature; closely linked with the mind.
notes: Symptom lists simplified and recalled with low confidence.

name: Mkhris pa (bile) disorders
description: Disturbance of bile: heat, fever, bitter taste, yellowish colouring, irritability; hot in nature.
notes: Symptom lists simplified and recalled with low confidence.

name: Bad kan (phlegm) disorders
description: Disturbance of phlegm: heaviness, dullness, poor digestion, cold and sluggishness; cold in nature.
notes: Symptom lists simplified and recalled with low confidence.

name: The four hundred and four diseases
description: Diseases counted as 4 × 101: karmic (yield only to Dharma), life-span (require treatment), spirit-caused (require ritual) and superficial (pass by themselves or with diet and behaviour).

name: The three roots of bad (greed, hatred, delusion)
description: In Sowa Rigpa the three poisons — desire, hatred and delusion — arising from ignorance are the causes of rlung, mkhris pa and bad kan respectively.

name: Clinging to an emptiness of annihilation (chad stong)
description: Taking the ultimate to be a mere nothingness, a non-affirming negation; for the Jonang an extreme that misses the emptiness endowed with all supreme aspects.
antidotes: recognition of the other-empty ultimate through the vajra-yoga

equivalents.note: all Madhyamaka schools reject nihilism, but the Jonang count the rangtong ultimate itself as this error, which the rangtong schools deny

name: The adventitious stains (glo bur gyi dri ma)
description: The conventional obscurations covering buddha-nature, which are other than it and separable from it; removing them uncovers qualities that were always present.
antidotes: hearing, reflection and meditation on the definitive meaning

name: Sectarian bias (phyogs 'dzin; ris su chad pa)
description: Partiality towards one's own school and contempt for others, which the Rimé masters regard as a cause of abandoning the Dharma and of the loss of lineages.
antidotes: receiving and respecting the teachings of all lineages
studying root texts through their Indian commentaries

name: Abandoning the Dharma (chos spong ba)
description: The grave fault of disparaging or rejecting any authentic teaching of the Buddha; the Rimé masters apply it to sectarian disparagement of other traditions.
notes: The fault is a general Mahāyāna category (saddharma-pratikṣepa); its Rimé application is recalled, the specific passage is not.
